notes.meaning: Paul instructs Titus to keep reminding believers to submit to government rulers and civil authorities in all lawful things. Christians should not be rebellious, but law-abiding citizens who are ready at any moment to do good in their communities. Faith in God strengthens our civil duties rather than canceling them.

Believers are told never to insult or speak evil of anyone, even when dealing with difficult rulers or harsh neighbors. Instead, they must be peaceful, gentle, and patient with all people rather than picking fights. Showing kindness to others reflects the humble character of Christ.

Paul reminds Christians that before knowing Christ, they were just as foolish, disobedient, and trapped by evil desires as anyone else. Unbelievers lived in envy, bitterness, and mutual hatred, unable to free themselves from sin. Remembering what we used to be keeps us humble and patient toward people who do not yet follow God.

God broke into human darkness by revealing His extraordinary goodness and love for humanity through Jesus Christ. Salvation began entirely with God's deep affection for mankind, not with anything good that people had to offer. His kindness reached down to rescue us when we could not rescue ourselves.

God saved us entirely because of His mercy, not because of any righteous deeds or good works we performed. He rescued us by giving us a new birth that cleanses the heart and by sending the Holy Spirit to make us new people. Good deeds are the fruit of being saved, never the price we pay for it.

differ.view: The washing of new birth refers to the spiritual cleansing produced by the Holy Spirit and the Word of God, not to water baptism.
The washing points to water baptism as an outward sign and seal of the inward spiritual cleansing done by the Holy Spirit.
Baptism is the means through which the Holy Spirit actively grants faith and causes the new birth.
The baptismal font is the visible instrument of regeneration, where grace is visibly sealed and deepened by God.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Baptism is an effective sacrament of salvation that actually washes away sins and brings about new birth in the soul.

notes.meaning: God did not hold back His Holy Spirit, but poured Him out richly upon believers through Jesus Christ. Jesus earned this blessing for His people through His death and resurrection. Every believer now has access to the full spiritual power and comfort the Spirit provides.

To be justified means that God freely pardons our sins and counts us righteous because of Jesus, completely by His unearned grace. Through this pardon, believers are adopted into God's family and become heirs who will inherit eternal life. This certain promise fills us with real hope as we look toward heaven.

Paul insists that the message of salvation by grace is completely trustworthy and should be taught constantly. Believers who trust in God are urged to throw themselves into doing good and practical deeds. These good actions are valuable because they bring genuine help to people around us.

Titus is told to avoid pointless debates, family tree arguments, and quarrelsome fights about the Old Testament law. These discussions do not help anyone grow in faith and are completely useless. Christians should turn away from endless arguing and focus on what builds up the church.

When a person causes factions and divides the church with false teaching, leaders must give him a first and second warning. If he refuses to repent and continues stirring up division, the church must separate from him and avoid his company. This protects the church from being torn apart.

A person who keeps stirring up division after two clear warnings shows that his mind is warped and trapped in sin. He stands self-condemned because he has heard the truth and still chosen to rebel against it. His own stubborn refusal to repent makes his guilt clear to everyone.

Paul tells Titus that he plans to send either Artemas or Tychicus to take over his duties on the island of Crete. As soon as the replacement arrives, Titus is to travel quickly to meet Paul in the city of Nicopolis, where Paul plans to stay during the winter. Paul cared deeply that the churches would never be left without good leadership.

Paul instructs Titus to assist Zenas the lawyer and Apollos by supplying whatever they need for their upcoming journey. Christians were expected to support traveling gospel workers with food, travel expenses, and lodging so their work would not be stopped. Sharing our resources helps spread the good news.

Believers must learn to practice good works by stepping in to meet the urgent daily needs of others. Working hard and helping the needy keeps a Christian's life from becoming useless or barren. Our faith should show itself in everyday acts of love and generous giving.

Paul sends warm greetings from all the coworkers who are with him to Titus and the whole church family. He asks Titus to greet those who love them in the shared bond of Christian faith. He closes the letter by praying that God's undeserved favor and blessing will rest on all of them.
